subject: Dedicated capacity offer: stepped-commit proposal & soft-floor options - Nyxera Therapeutics
messages:
From: Alex Sampson <alex.sampson@nyxera.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@nyxera.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity discussion follow-up

Evelyn —

Thanks for the quick call this morning. To follow up, my team asked for a clear set of commitment options we can take to procurement: cluster sizes, minimum sustained GPUs, and a realistic ramp schedule (we prefer stepped commitments so we don't over-commit early). Also include any warm-standby / burst options and how those affect cost.

Can you send over a concise options sheet we can circulate? Procurement would like a single-page summary plus a deeper appendix.

Appreciate it,
Alex
Head of AI Platforms
Nyxera Therapeutics
[Attachment: -]
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Sampson <alex.sampson@nyxera.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity discussion follow-up

Alex —

Attached is a two-page summary and an appendix with numbers. Top-level options (summary):

1) Pilot lane (Conservative) — 16 A100-equivalent GPUs
   - Minimum guaranteed: 4 GPUs (soft-floor)
   - Typical sustained concurrency target: 50 QPS (model dependent)
   - Ramp: weeks 0-4: 4 -> 8 GPUs, weeks 5-12: 8 -> 16 GPUs (triggered by 70% utilization)
   - Use-case: proof-of-concept + low-latency staging

2) Growth lane (Balanced) — 64 GPUs
   - Minimum guaranteed: 20 GPUs (hard-floor, billing applies)
   - Ramp: quarter 1: 20 -> 40, quarter 2: 40 -> 64 (automated scaling windows)
   - Bursting: +20% ephemeral burst capacity for 8 hours/day (metered)

3) Enterprise lane (Throughput) — 256 GPUs
   - Minimum guaranteed: 80 GPUs (hard-floor, multi-region options)
   - Ramp: staged: 0-3 months: 80 baseline, 3-9 months: phased increments to 256 by agreed milestones
   - Includes dedicated pre-warmed lanes, hot-standby for DR and priority routing

Pricing note: soft-floor vs hard-floor changes billing. Soft-floor (pilot) has a smaller guaranteed minimum and a blended overage rate; hard-floor is fully committed and has step discounts. Appendix has per-GPU effective CPM and expected token burn examples.

I've copied Ben and Marissa for implementation and SLA/Ops notes. Attached PDF has the timeline charts and an editable MA-plan spreadsheet.

Next step: if procurement wants a single-row executive summary, we can produce a 1-page memo and a sign-off clause for the DocuSign packet.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Nyxera_Dedicated_Options_v2.pdf]
From: Priya Rao <priya.rao@nyxera.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Alex Sampson <alex.sampson@nyxera.com>
Cc: procurement@nyxera.com
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 10:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity discussion follow-up

Thanks Evelyn — looks good. A few clarifying Qs from procurement:

- For the Growth lane, is the 20 GPU minimum billable even if unused each month? (Procurement preference is predictable OPEX)
- For Pilot soft-floor, what triggers the blended overage rate versus hard invoice?
- Can you provide a sample schedule that demonstrates the quarterly ramp with milestone gates (we want to align payments to milestones)?

Also, can you confirm what logs and audit artifacts you provide (retention window) and whether we can host the private control plane in our GCP VPC? Security will need that for compliance sign-off.

Thanks,
Priya
Contracts & Procurement
Nyxera Therapeutics
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Rao <priya.rao@nyxera.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Alex Sampson <alex.sampson@nyxera.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 08:44:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity discussion follow-up

Priya — quick answers inline:

- Growth lane minimum (20 GPUs) is billable as a committed minimum. We can include a quarterly reconciliation clause: if usage is >120% of committed baseline we apply step increases; if <60% for two consecutive quarters, we offer a one-time rebaseline (with notice).

- Pilot soft-floor: billing is split: guaranteed 4 GPUs billed at committed rate; additional consumed capacity billed at on-demand price (blended rate applied monthly). We can convert to a temporary trial credit for month 1 to reduce risk.

- Milestone schedule: see attached MA-plan spreadsheet (we built a payment ramp tied to technical acceptance criteria). Example: 30% payment at pilot activation, 30% at validated throughput (70% utilization), 40% on full roll to baseline.

- Security/compliance: we support a VPC-hosted control plane and can enable 12-month audit log retention (longer retention available as add-on). SOC2 evidence and an architecture diagram are in the appendix.

Also flagging Soojin for quant & runtime sizing details if Nyxera asks for a different GPU family (e.g., H100 vs A100).

Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Nyxera_MA-Plan.xlsx]
From: Alex Sampson <alex.sampson@nyxera.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@nyxera.com>, procurement@nyxera.com
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 14:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity discussion follow-up

Ben / Evelyn —

This is helpful. Procurement likes the stepped ramp approach and the milestone-linked payments. Two asks before we run to our CFO:

1) Can Redwood offer a 90-day credit buffer on the pilot soft-floor (month 1 free + 2 months credit) to de-risk the PoC?
2) For enterprise lane: provide options for a staggered multi-region footprint (primary on GCP us-west1, DR on us-east1) and a short note on cross-region egress effects on billing.

If we can get those in the one-page summary and a lightly redlined SLA, we should be able to move to signatures next week.

Alex
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Sampson <alex.sampson@nyxera.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity discussion follow-up

Alex —

We can do the pilot buffer: month 1 credit + two-month deferred billing (applied as a billing credit over first 90 days). I'll add a short clause to the MA-plan.

For the enterprise multi-region split, high-level:
- Primary: GCP us-west1, DR: GCP us-east1.
- Dedicated cluster mapping: baseline (80 GPUs) split 70/30 by region for failover; full expansion to 256 will be provisioned efficiently with cross-region pre-warmed nodes.
- Cross-region egress: we will charge measured egress on inter-region replication; recommended pattern is model weights via artifact store with one-time sync (reduction) and token traffic routed to the nearest region. We will include an estimate in the appendix.

SLA redline: attach lightweight SLA with availability targets and a rollback/fallback policy to Hosted API if Dedicated region experiences sustained degradation. DocuSign-ready packet will include the stepped payment schedule and the credit buffer.

Looping Soojin for the runtime-quant notes and Ben for final commercial items. If Ok, we'll produce the single-page exec summary and post it to the HubSpot deal.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Solutions Architecture
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Nyxera_SLA_Draft.docx]
